message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 40 AAPL @ limit $222.90 — filled at $222.90, total $8,916.00.

**Summary of what I did and why.** I read Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01), checked the latest news, and pulled a live quote before acting. The fundamentals support a modest add: total net sales rose 2% to $391,035 million in FY2024 from $383,285 million, operating income grew to $123,216 million from $114,301 million, and Services revenue climbed 13% to $96,169 million with total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%. Net income, however, *declined* to $93,736 million in FY2024 from $96,995 million in FY2023 — a 3.4% drop driven almost entirely by a one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge related to the European Commission's State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not by operating deterioration; diluted EPS was $6.08 vs. $6.13. News flow was neutral-to-constructive and quiet: shares were "little changed" around $222 with analysts weighing iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, supplier builds described as steady into December, and holiday-quarter estimates unchanged — no catalyst forcing either urgency or avoidance. With the stock at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and the pre-tax earnings trend intact, I bought 40 shares at a $222.90 limit — about 0.1% above the market, satisfying the "close to market" requirement — for $8,916, which is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily cap, using existing cash so no money left the account. I deliberately kept the position small given the headline net income decline and the unresolved DOJ/EU antitrust and DMA matters disclosed in the filing.
